import sys

def count_permutations(n, k, p):
    MOD = p
    
    # dp[i][j] will store the number of valid permutations of length i ending with a run of length j
    dp = [[0] * (k + 1) for _ in range(n + 1)]
    
    # Base case: There's one way to arrange a single element with a run of length 1
    dp[1][1] = 1
    
    # Fill the dp table
    for i in range(2, n + 1):
        for j in range(1, k + 1):
            # Case 1: Extend the previous run
            if j > 1:
                dp[i][j] += dp[i - 1][j - 1]
            
            # Case 2: Start a new run of length 1
            dp[i][1] += dp[i - 1][j]
        
        # Take modulo p
        for j in range(1, k + 1):
            dp[i][j] %= MOD
    
    # Sum up all valid permutations of length n
    result = sum(dp[n]) % MOD
    
    return result

    MOD = p
    
    # dp[i][j] will store the number of valid permutations of length i ending with a run of length j
    dp = [[0] * (k + 1) for _ in range(n + 1)]
    
    # Base case: There's one way to arrange a single element permutation
    dp[1][1] = 1

            # Case 2: Start a new run with the current element

            dp[i][1] %= MOD
    
    # Sum up all valid permutations of length n
    result = sum(dp[n]) % MOD
    return result
